newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 13.

text.p: HODPODARSKE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry's special organisational department recieves each month from financial institutions tens of announcements of "unusual business", more often than not meaning illegal operations.

- The Automobile Imports Association announced Friday that Fiat Punto had the best sales of any car in the Czech Republic in 1996. The most successful importer on the Czech market was the Opel corporation followed by Volkswagen and Ford.

- An attorney for Vladimir Stehlik, Jiri Teryngel has not ruled out the possibility that an agreement between his client and the Finance Ministry over the return of Stehlik's shares of Poldi Steel will be concluded this week.

- For this year, 8.01 billion crowns will be granted to the agriculture sector, a 21 percent increase over last year. Nearly half of this money, 3.8 billion crowns, will go to the Promotive Grant Farming and Forest Fund (PGRLF), while the remaining 53 percent will go directly to farmers.

- The establishment of import quotas for Czech goods imported to Slovakia, which was discussed at the end of 1996, was unsuccessful, and the Slovak side is considering further possibilities for regulating imports.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Although the government knows that various corporations successfully evade taxes, officials at the Finance Ministry insist that they can do nothing to stop it without causing a decline on the capital market.

- Subsidiaries of Skoda Plzen, Tatra and Skoda Liaz, which have been struggling in a crisis state for the past five years, will have radical cuts this year. Both companies will lay off approximately 800 workers.
PRAVO - During the first week of this year, the crown strengthened on the interbank exchange market by more than one percentage point.
- Union Bank Ostrava (UB) predicts that its investment placed into Evrobanka, Ekoagrobanka, Bankovni Doma Skala and into the integration of these banks into UB will have paid off in three years.
